minutes.headline: Sewer Commission leaned toward denying a Northfield Road sewer extension, citing the wastewater plan; developer to return
minutes.summary: After educational videos on flushables and grease, the commission heard a resident on a possible privilege fee for a lot on Josselyn Street. Most of the meeting went to a request to change the sewer service area at 175 Northfield Road, where the chair recommended denial or tabling absent proof of need. The DPW director updated on Lancaster Ave, I&I, generators and SCADA, members volunteered as project champions, and a member's attendance remarks drew expressions of support.

public_comment.topic: Asked for leniency on a possible betterment fee for 51 Josselyn Street; told it would be a privilege fee payable over 10 years if connected.

what_happened.line: The commission took no vote on a request to change the sewer service area at 175 Northfield Road; the developer is to return.
A motion to deny going down Northfield Road was withdrawn after no second.
The applicant's engineer is to meet the building inspector on the seven-lot layout and come back at the next meeting.
A resident was told a connection at 51 Josselyn Street would carry a privilege fee equal to the last betterment, payable over 10 years.
The commission agreed to invite the I&I consultant to revisit scope and to drop the Fitchburg adder from February billing unless costs are identified.

why_it_matters: A sewer extension on Northfield Road could add connections the town may have to tie in at its own cost, which would fall on sewer rates and the town budget, mostly taxes.
Homeowners asked to connect to the sewer, as on Josselyn Street, face a privilege fee that can be spread over 10 years, and none has been waived so far.
watch_next: The next regular meeting on the 11th at the DPW, where the 175 Northfield Road developer is due to return.
The FinCom FY15 budget presentation on 27 March.
